band_change_evidence_test.reason: FAIL. Multiple independent sources were located — Axios, CNBC, TechCrunch and Data Center Dynamics — but none above tier 3. The reported Senate scrutiny of the Nvidia arrangement was found only in secondary coverage; no primary congressional document was obtained. Groq cannot be verified at tier 4 in either direction.

key_evidence: Groq is not the company the index entry describes. In December 2025 it did a roughly $20 billion licensing deal with Nvidia under which around 90% of its employees moved to Nvidia, including chief executive Jonathan Ross and president Sunny Madra.
It is still operating. A new chief executive, former finance chief Simon Edwards, runs it, and it confirmed a $650 million raise in June 2026 and is re-staffing.
The one clearly positive fact is how staff were treated: departing employees were paid cash for all vested shares. In a transaction where they had no leverage, that is a real choice.
No responsible-AI policy, safety commitment, workforce data or failure disclosure of any kind was located. Thirty-six of 40 subdimensions rest on absence of disclosure.
No source above tier 3 was obtained. Groq cannot be verified at tier 4 in either direction, which is the strongest argument that a tier-4-level placeholder was never publishable for it.

evidence.source: Axios on the Nvidia and Groq arrangement
